answer: Each agent posts a skin-in-the-game bond against a per-identity cost curve, so a Sybil swarm scales linearly in money: a hundred identities cost a hundred bonds, and reputation accrues only to bonds that survive audits. A fresh identity behaves like raw quartz, cheap but worthless until cut and graded. Peers grade in public, and a suspected cluster is penalized as one flat mesa, not many small hills. Attestations route through a random prism so colluders cannot map partners. The attacker's payoff stays negative, since forfeited bonds exceed any subsidy a captured vote could yield.
